cases.customer_question: Should the Class 1 RF retest use 3 dBm or 13 dBm TX power?
question_variants: Which TX power should be used for Class 1 RF testing?
Should we follow 3 dBm or 13 dBm in DUT mode?
What transmit power should be used in the corrected RF report?
Can Class 1 RF testing pass at 3 dBm?
cases.actual_issue: The team was unsure whether the corrected Class 1 RF test should use 3 dBm or 13 dBm because different materials or interpretations pointed to different TX power values.
cases.plain_english_explanation: After deciding the product should be tested as Class 1, the next issue was the exact transmit power setting. The consultant said to follow the customer’s DUT operation procedure, which stated 3 dBm. A related previous product had also passed Class 1 RF testing at 3 dBm.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant instructed the team to use the 3 dBm setting because the customer-submitted operation procedure explicitly specified 3 dBm. The consultant also relied on precedent from a related product that passed Class 1 RF testing with 3 dBm output.
cases.decision_logic: When RF test setup values are unclear, the documented DUT operation procedure and validated previous evidence should drive the test configuration.
cases.final_recommendation: Use Class 1 / 3 dBm for the corrected RF test and report.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Using the wrong TX power can make the report inconsistent with the DUT operating instructions and may require another correction or retest.
